eligible_source_payloads.label: Gather deadwood
eligible_source_payloads._why_game_f1: GAME-F1 (Gate F full run, candidate 453107fb). This node stood at (44, -24), 2.3 m OUTSIDE data/config/village_boundary.json's outline after that line was rerouted on 2026-08-30 (OP-0830-1 and the straddle fix the same day). The fence is a hard StaticBody3D, so the chapter's own first gathering lesson sent the player out through their own village gate and back for this stop, and a player who has not yet found the gate key could not reach it at all. Moved 4.3 m inward to the nearest point that is inside the line, at least 3 m clear of it, at least 4 m from every other node, and still outside the practice cluster's own 15 m disc. The item, amount, label, model and order are unchanged, so the village gathering budget is untouched -- which matters, because with this node and its sibling unreachable the reachable stone in the village (6) fell short of the 8 that progression.json's home.required_pieces actually costs. tests/test_village_boundary.gd now checks every village-area harvest node, so a future reroute of the fence fails a test instead of stranding a node.

eligible_source_payloads.label: Gather deadwood
eligible_source_payloads._why_grandpas_village_r2_2026_09_11: The R1 production square-arrival pair proved this exact persistent deadwood visual stands on the camera-to-well axis as a black foreground shrub, obscuring the civic square by day and night. A committed-bake audit found no deadfall scatter crossing that composition, so changing a scatter footprint would remove unrelated vegetation and would not touch the demonstrated obstruction. Keep the node, position, yield, order, model and interaction; reduce only its rendered scale 0.22 -> 0.12 so it remains a readable deadwood gatherable without blocking the well/path/NPC composition.

eligible_source_payloads.label: Prise loose stones
eligible_source_payloads._why_game_f5_stone: GAME-F5, RESCOPED and measured on the played path 2026-08-31 (lane ralph/GATE-F-LEG-S03). GAME-F5 reported the village gathering budget as short against a camp+floor+wall+door+roof+3-bed bill the game stopped asking for; against the real bill (camp + one creature_bed = 18 wood / 8 stone / 18 fiber) wood and fiber clear comfortably. STONE does not. The village authors exactly three stone nodes at 3 each = 9, against a camp that costs 8 -- a one-node margin, and a real S03 run measured what that costs: two of the three nodes paid out, the sweep ended with 6 stone, the camp could not be armed (the run reported input_context=build_catalogue where it wanted build_placement, which reads like a build-menu defect and is an empty satchel), `home_built` never set, and the sleep and feed rungs never ran. Wood came in at 24 against 18 and fiber at 28 against 18 in the same sweep, so stone was the only binding constraint. 3 -> 4 puts the authored stone budget at 12 against 8, a margin proportionate to the other two, and survives a single missed node. Every number in this file is TUNABLE by its own header; this is the smallest change that makes the opening's build rung affordable in practice rather than only on paper. Mirrored into tests/fixtures/band_split_baseline/harvest.json per that fixture's TRACKED MIRROR policy.

eligible_source_payloads.label: Prise out rootstone
eligible_source_payloads._why:
T5-CADENCE, fixing T4-REGIONS' fifth-ranked chapter gap head-on: 'The resource ladder goes backwards. Band 2 introduces rootstone + ironwood; band 3 drops to wood/fiber/stone/berries.' MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC §10 and items.json's own `rootstone` comment agree there are exactly two tier materials in the whole biome, Rootstone then Ironwood, and a band that ships neither is a band whose economy is band 1's. Three deposits here and four Ironwood on the north bank (orders 3027-3030) put band 3 back on the ladder without turning it into a second Old Quarry: band 2 keeps five deposits and band 4 keeps ten trees, so the ladder still rises.

SITED IN THE HAULAGE SPILL (props.json order 3005), not in open meadow, and that is the whole reason this is honest content rather than a number correction. items.json says Rootstone 'comes only from deep seams -- warrens, old quarry faces', and there is no seam in the river country; what there IS, is Team Tether's haul road out of Stone & Root. This is their load, off the sled and on the ground. Pickaxe-gated like all stone through `gathered_with` on the ITEM, never on the node.
